items.title: A fresh install starts with the code graph unbuilt, so code search and impact analysis are dark until a cron eventually fires
items.body:
Reported from one install, reproduced on a completely fresh one.

## Observed on a new install

```
get_code_graph_freshness ->
  available: false, indexStatus: "missing", indexedFileCount: 0,
  lastIndexedAt: null, lastError: null
  message: "Code graph has not been built yet for this workspace."

find_related_tests { filePath: "apps/web/lib/inference/local-model-policy.ts" } ->
  success: false, error: "Code graph unavailable"
```

Zero code-graph mentions in an hour of portal logs. The tables exist (`CodeGraphIndexState`, `CodeGraphFileHash`) and are empty.

## Root cause

The graph is populated by `apps/web/lib/queue/functions/code-graph-reconcile.ts`, which is driven by an Inngest **`cron`** schedule. Nothing builds it at install time, so a fresh install waits for the first scheduled tick. Until then, `search_code_graph`, `find_related_tests` and change-impact analysis are unavailable.

This is **not** structural: the source ships with the install (`dpf_dpf-source-code` contains `apps`, `packages`, `docs`, and the portal sees `/workspace` and `/app/apps/web-src`). The material is present; the index is simply never seeded.

## Why it matters more than a slow first tick

Every external agent connecting to a fresh install pays a real cost. An agent reported it this way, and its reasoning was correct:

> The MCP code graph is currently unbuilt, so its related-test lookup correctly refused to guess. Per the repository contract, that expands verification: I'm using colocated and contract-level tests plus the exhaustive exact-tree gate instead of treating missing graph advice as evidence.

That is the right behaviour and the tool contract is sound — refusing to guess beats fabricating test advice. But the fallback is **exhaustive** verification, so every agent on a new install runs the expensive path until a cron happens to fire. Multiply that across the agent fleet and it is a substantial, invisible tax.

The same file already recognises the stakes:

> "The scheduled code-graph reconcile is not succeeding. A stale code graph degrades code search and impact analysis across Build Studio and the EA surfaces until it recovers."

## Proposed

1. **Seed the graph during install**, or enqueue a build immediately on first boot, so the capability is live when the operator and their agents first connect.
2. **Surface the state to agents**, not just to `get_code_graph_freshness` when asked. An agent that never calls the freshness tool discovers the gap only when a lookup fails.
3. Distinguish *"never built"* from *"stale"* in operator-facing surfaces — `indexStatus: "missing"` with `lastError: null` currently reads as benign, and on a fresh install it is the normal state rather than a fault.

Related shape: this is the third capability found dark on a fresh install this cycle, after the local provider shipping disabled and profile-gated inngest starving the router. Worth asking which other capabilities depend on a scheduled tick that has never fired.

Provenance: reported from another install, reproduced on reset/dogfood cycle 4 (image v2026.08.23-cycle4.1).

The platform-support watchlist D8 records this exact fresh-install symptom as fixed; this install observed pre-upgrade bytes.

items.title: portal-migrate-boot watchdog test has a wall-clock margin too tight for a loaded gate host
items.body:
## Problem

`apps/web/lib/self-upgrade/portal-migrate-boot.test.ts:296` asserts `expect(r.durationMs).toBeLessThan(2_500)` for the "portable process group" watchdog test. The watchdog itself is a 2000 ms timeout, so the assertion allows only a **500 ms** margin for spawning a real subprocess, running `portal-migrate-boot.sh`, killing the process group, and collecting the result.

That margin is too thin for the local-CI vitest stage, which runs with `--maxWorkers=4` on a host that is also running Docker. Observed 2026-08-25 on `fix/coworker-envelope-owner-inbox` @ `c08b33dd345f`:

```
FAIL lib/self-upgrade/portal-migrate-boot.test.ts > portal-migrate-boot.sh (BI-5322D025) > terminates a hung boot subprocess with the 'portable process group' watchdog
AssertionError: expected 2559 to be less than 2500
```

59 ms over. `Test Files 1 failed | 2948 passed`, `Tests 1 failed | 25243 passed`.

Re-running the same file in isolation on the same host and the same commit passes **9/9**, which is the signature of host-pressure flake rather than a real regression. The failing branch touches nothing under `lib/self-upgrade/`.

## Why it matters

The local-CI gate is SHA-bound and must be PASS before a runtime-code push. A timing flake in one unrelated test invalidates a whole gate run — roughly 25,000 tests and about 28 minutes of host time — and forces a full re-run. It also teaches agents that a red gate can be ignored, which is the more expensive damage: it erodes the "the gate is the verdict" discipline that `pregate:status` exists to protect.

## Scope

Make the watchdog assertion robust under load without weakening what it actually proves. The test's real claims are that the boot **timed out** (`r.timedOut === true`), that it exited **124**, and that it was killed rather than left hanging — those stay exact. Only the wall-clock ceiling needs to tolerate scheduler pressure.

Options to weigh:
- Widen the ceiling to a load-tolerant bound (e.g. watchdog + 1500 ms) and keep the exact `timedOut` / status assertions as the real signal.
- Derive the ceiling from the configured watchdog timeout rather than a second hardcoded literal, so the two cannot drift.
- Sweep sibling timing assertions in the same file and in `lib/self-upgrade/` for the same too-thin-margin shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- The watchdog test passes under the local-CI vitest stage at `--maxWorkers=4` on a loaded host.
- The test still fails if the watchdog genuinely stops terminating the process group, or if the exit status is not 124.
- No wall-clock ceiling in the file is a bare literal that can drift from the watchdog timeout it is derived from.
- Any sibling assertion found with the same shape is fixed in the same pass or explicitly listed as out of scope.

Observed during BI-7CB2CCDE (WC-635FCF78). Related: BI-5322D025 introduced the watchdog under test.
items.scopeRationale: A flaky assertion in the shared local-CI vitest stage fails unrelated PRs across the whole platform, so the defect is platform-wide rather than archetype-specific.

items.title: `search_specs_and_plans` returns zero results on a runtime-host install, silently defeating the pre-filing overlap check
items.body:
**Observed 2026-08-26** on this development installation (`D:\DPF`, purpose `evolve-dpf`).

`search_specs_and_plans` returns `{"results":[]}` for every query, including single common words:
- `"interaction shape graph"` → `[]` (the spec exists on `main` at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-interaction-shape-graph-and-design-shaping-design.md`)
- `"lexicon"` → `[]`
- `"design"` → `[]` — a word in nearly every spec filename in the corpus

**Root cause hypothesis (unverified).** The tool reads `docs/superpowers/` relative to the install root. Per this host's own declared identity, *"Source — none: This directory holds installed runtime assets and no source"* — so the tree it searches is absent. The source checkout lives separately (here: `D:\DPF-source-root`, which does contain the corpus).

**Why this matters more than it looks.** `AGENTS.md` §5 requires checking for an existing design before writing a new one, and §1 requires grounding new work in existing platform work. `search_specs_and_plans` is the tool for that check. Returning `[]` is indistinguishable from "no prior art exists", so the failure mode is silent and biases toward creating duplicate specs and parallel substrate — the exact outcome §1 exists to prevent. An empty result should never be mistaken for a clean overlap check.

**Expected behaviour.** Either resolve the corpus from the configured source checkout, or fail loudly (`corpus_unavailable`) so the caller knows the check did not run. Never return an empty success.

**Workaround used.** Fell back to `list_backlog_items` for the overlap check and to direct `grep` over `D:\DPF-source-root` for the substrate check.

**Related.** Two other read tools on this install are worth checking for the same root cause: any tool resolving `docs/` or repo paths from the install root rather than a source checkout.
items.scopeRationale: Affects the governed MCP tool surface on every consumer/runtime-host installation, independent of archetype or organization.

items.title: Enforce Workroom WIP, progress SLOs, and durable-wait liveness
items.body:
## Problem

Continuous machine activity is not producing proportional delivery: only four PRs landed in seven hours. Workrooms do not distinguish durable waiting from dead sessions, and no progress SLO prevents days of low-movement activity behind bottlenecks.

## Scope

Project running, waiting-for-gate, ready-to-resume, terminal, and stale from existing Workroom/lease/TaskRun evidence. Enforce bottleneck WIP policy and emit stale-wait/low-throughput attention using existing telemetry and attention substrate.

## Acceptance criteria

- Queued lease evidence prevents false Workroom reaping.
- Heavy lanes expose executing, next-ready, and dormant counts.
- Progress SLOs cover oldest wait, no-transition duration, throughput, and abandonment.
- A breach creates one deduplicated attention/escalation item with an actionable reason.
- Operator view distinguishes productive processing from polling/busy noise.
- Lists remain cursor-bounded at platform scale.

Parent: BI-7C1F43E3.
Depends on durable wait-state events for final end-to-end verification.

items.title: A consumer install gives an external agent 248 MCP tools and zero orientation — no AGENTS.md, no README, no skills
items.body:
**Investigation and design decision, not a defect fix.** The operator's question is the right frame: *what is an external agent supposed to do when the source is not installed?*

## What a consumer install actually contains

Verified on a fresh consumer install: runtime configuration, compose files, startup/stop scripts, monitoring, safety tools, and MCP configuration are present. Source-oriented guidance is absent.

- No `AGENTS.md`, README, or source-agent skill directories.
- `.mcp.json` is present and correctly references the bearer token without embedding it.
- A connecting agent receives a broad MCP surface and no compact statement of the business-operating contract.

The source repository carries contributor doctrine for worktrees, gates, PRs, and DCO. That doctrine does not belong wholesale on a production business install.

## The decision

Choose the source-free orientation shape:

- a static install file;
- a versioned, principal/tier/install-aware served contract;
- or both, with a generated local file only as a pointer to the served contract.

The external-agent operating-contract design selected the third shape in `DI-C75C83499B57`: the served runtime contract is canonical; the tiny generated pointer exists only for local discovery and carries a version/digest and fail-closed stop rule.

## Constraints

- install-mode aware;
- token-tier and principal aware;
- reachable before first action;
- no copied contributor doctrine, static tool catalog, secret, or business record;
- compatible with MCP/A2A clients that never inspect local files;
- implemented without competing with the broader umbrella `BI-9549EE48`.

Provenance: from-scratch reset/dogfood cycle 3, automated consumer-install finding.

## Interaction-shape correction — 2026-08-24

The authenticated operating profile must distinguish two use shapes over one agent/work substrate. Customer installations default to **business operations**: business outcomes, Work Cases, authorized domain surfaces, WWWD organization judgment, WSID professional judgment, and business outcome–anchored Workrooms. Repository, worktree, PR, CI, and Build Studio concepts stay out of the primary path.

**Platform development** is default only when the primary purpose is `evolve-dpf`, and is an explicit alternate only when `evolve-dpf` is a confirmed secondary purpose. Purpose does not grant authority. Environment class controls caution, host profile controls source location, and token/grant intersection controls actions. A source-free runtime coordinates development through MCP but sends source edits to a separate governed checkout.

The P0 wire contract now projects the default/available shape, secondary purposes, WWWD/WSID/WWMD decision routing, and development source location. The previous semantic approval at `8e0285309965` is superseded and fresh independent review/baseline is required.

items.title: Local-CI pre-product infrastructure failures poison immutable gate evidence
items.body:
## Problem

The exact-tree local-CI runner can fail before any product command executes (observed while resetting the disposable PostgreSQL database during a database shutdown). The gate currently maps that early runner exit to generic `failed`, binds a 24-hour reusable product-failure receipt to the immutable integration-tree identity, and refuses every honest retry of the unchanged tree. `pregate:status` simultaneously reports that no failing command was recorded and the diff has no failure evidence.

Observed evidence: lease `NPEL-661F181FD0`, evidence `cmt9eeigc02ej01qvqndk8o91`, integration-gate key `a6d645ae4937aeef0b0ad30419eb7a013dfd9b264c315a7a527f4041992b9652`.

## Scope

In:
- `scripts/local-ci-runner.mjs` early/pre-product-command outcome contract.
- `scripts/gate-worktree.mjs` evidence classification and audit-preserving retry authorization.
- Focused runner/gate tests and operator documentation.

Out:
- Nonproduction lease scheduling, durable TaskRun wait/resume, environment-lease models, or resource-lane policy.
- Weakening or bypassing product gates.
- Editing installed runtime assets.

## Acceptance criteria

- No product command executed means no reusable product-failure receipt is minted.
- Infrastructure-inconclusive evidence remains immutable, visible, and auditable.
- A corrected retry of the same immutable integration tree is authorized after infrastructure recovery.
- Genuine product-command failures remain reusable and continue to refuse duplicate execution.
- Tests reproduce the PostgreSQL-shutdown-before-command case, the same-tree retry, and the genuine product-failure reuse case.
- Source checks, exact-tree CI, DCO, protected PR, official release, and live verification remain required.

## Dependencies

Blocks: BI-SIG-463E478D exact-tree gate and the downstream WordPress delivery chain.
Related but non-overlapping: BI-MCP-EFF-0285909C durable capacity wait/resume and BI-9DC21917 control-plane watchdog hysteresis.
items.scopeRationale: Cross-cutting exact-tree CI evidence semantics and retry authorization affect every platform contribution, independent of organization or archetype.

items.title: A .mcp.json naming a non-loopback endpoint sends the MCP bearer token to that host unchecked (CodeQL alert 388)
items.body:
**Source:** CodeQL `js/file-access-to-http` ("File data in outbound network request", CWE-200, medium), alert 388 on `main` @ 853068f. Sink `scripts/lib/mcp-client.mjs:65` (the request URL); source `scripts/host-resource-runner.mjs:133` (`readFileSync(.mcp.json)`).

**Defect.** `readMcpConnection` in `scripts/host-resource-runner.mjs` falls back to reading `.mcp.json` when `DPF_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN` is unset, and passes `mcpServers.dpf.url` straight to `mcpCall` together with the `dpfmcp_...` bearer token from the same file. The URL is never checked. `.mcp.json` is ambient state — gitignored, copied between worktrees by `scripts/sync-mcp-worktrees.ps1`, writable by anything with the checkout — so a copied-in, stale or tampered file silently redirects a live read/write/admin credential to whatever host it names. That is uncontrolled credential disclosure, not a connection failure. Every other MCP caller in `scripts/` (`gate-worktree.mjs`, `local-ci-bounded-build.mjs`, `pregate.mjs`) resolves the endpoint from `DPF_MCP_URL` or the loopback constant; this reader was the only one taking it from disk.

**Fix.** `isAllowedMcpEndpoint()` added to `scripts/lib/mcp-client.mjs` — accepts only `127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `[::1]` over http/https, and rejects a credentials-in-authority redirect such as `http://127.0.0.1@example.com/api/mcp/v1` where the loopback literal is the userinfo and the real host is remote. `readMcpConnection` runs the file-resolved endpoint through it and **stops** on a non-loopback host (AGENTS.md §1 — a refusal is a stop, not a fall-through to the default). `DPF_MCP_URL` is stated operator intent and stays unnarrowed, so a genuinely remote portal is still reachable.

Covered by tests in `scripts/host-resource-runner.test.mjs` (CI-covered via the Repo Guard Loop; `scripts/lib/mcp-client.test.mjs` is held out of CI by `scripts/ci-policy-test-inventory-allowlist.txt`, so the guard's coverage rides with the reader). Rule documented in `docs/architecture/mcp-tool-authorization-runbook.md`.
items.scopeRationale: Gate-script credential handling — applies to every install and every delivery surface, not to one archetype.

items.title: Make local-model setup and management genuinely local and in-product
items.body:
## Problem

The local-provider detail route applies cloud-account questions to Docker Model Runner, reports installed storage as 0 GB because its OpenAI list adapter discards DMR size metadata, and stubs install/delete actions so they fail into terminal-copy instructions. A non-technical operator therefore cannot trust or manage the local-model state from the screen that claims to manage it.

Observed on `/platform/ai/providers/local` at image revision `d104cd37c99ef85c8f8df5acfcd267bf1ff446a7`. The attached operator screenshot shows "Copy the pull command, run it in your terminal"; the live DMR native `GET /models` reports Nomic at 260.86 MiB and Hugging Face Qwen3.8 27B at 17.66 GiB while the portal adapter maps every model size to zero.

Docker's supported DMR API provides `POST /models/create`, `GET /models`, and `DELETE /models/{namespace}/{name}`: https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner/api-reference/

## Scope

In:
- Tailor provider detail UX by provider locality: local/ollama must not ask for account class, provider training terms, DPAs, or enabled cloud processing regions.
- Read DMR-native model metadata and show honest per-model and total on-disk size, with an explicit unavailable state rather than 0 GB when the runtime cannot report it.
- Replace catalog Copy controls with permission-gated in-product Install actions, observable progress, success/failure state, and automatic discover/profile refresh.
- Make confirmed Remove call the supported local management API and refresh the canonical installed/routing state after success.
- Explain capability impact before deleting a model used for embeddings or routing; confirmation remains required.
- If a legacy local runtime lacks management endpoints, show an honest unsupported/update-needed state; never ask the operator to run a terminal command.
- Refactor the oversized `OllamaManagement` surface into a typed local-model adapter/view-model plus focused UI pieces while behavior is protected by tests.
- Add measured UX-fit evidence for the exact UI diff and update user-facing/operator documentation impacted by the change.

Out:
- New provider, model, or database substrate.
- Generic host-shell execution from the web container.
- Automatically deleting an installed model without an explicit confirmation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Local provider pages do not render "Account type", "No training on company data", cloud-region, DPA, or equivalent cloud-contract declarations.
- Cloud provider pages retain those trust/account controls.
- The two live models above render non-zero sizes and the summary reflects their real aggregate size; unavailable metadata never renders as 0 GB.
- Clicking Install performs the pull inside DPF, reports progress/outcome, then makes the model visible/routable without a manual Refresh step.
- Clicking confirmed Remove performs the deletion inside DPF; the removed row disappears and discovery/profile state is reconciled.
- No local-model happy-path or failure copy tells the operator to run a terminal, PowerShell, shell script, or Docker command.
- Server actions keep existing authorization, validate model references, and call only the configured local DMR base URL.
- Regression tests are red before implementation and cover local/cloud form branching, metadata mapping, pull, delete, legacy-endpoint failure, and reconciliation.
- Functional verification drives the route against the governed local install in dark and light themes at desktop and narrow viewport.

Dependencies: independent; extends the existing local provider and model-management substrate.

## Governed 27B timeout correction (operator clarification, 2026-08-24)

The trustworthy local-reviewer route deliberately uses Qwen3.8 27B even when it is slower. A readiness preview omitted `DPF_LOCAL_INFERENCE_TIMEOUT_MS`, silently inherited the 120,000 ms adapter default, and then treated the timeout as a reason to consider a smaller model. That is configuration drift, not model-selection evidence.

Additional acceptance criteria:
- One canonical policy identifies Qwen3.8 27B as the governed high-trust local reviewer route; a UI `recommended` label cannot silently override it.
- The effective local inference timeout for that route is a bounded 600,000 ms, and task/worker/lease lifetimes cannot expire first.
- Runtime/provider diagnostics expose the effective timeout and served context so a preview cannot claim the source setting without proving the running value.
- Tests cover unset/default and explicit 600,000 ms behavior, including a slow local response that exceeds 120 seconds without being aborted.
- A timeout is reported as infrastructure/performance evidence; it never lowers model quality policy or authorizes a smaller reviewer automatically.
- Existing 8B installations may remain available for appropriate low-cost routes, but they do not replace the 27B governed-reviewer route.

Blocks recurrence of the BI-F0715C9C reviewer-bootstrap failure; implementation remains separate from that immutable readiness-repair envelope.

items.title: Coworker opening briefing relabels team-held attention as owner review work
items.body:
## Problem

On a fresh local install, the Workspace owner surface and the AI coworker opening briefing make contradictory claims from the same attention feed:

- Workspace: **0 things need you today** and **Your digital team is handling 51 items — no action needed**.
- Coworker opening briefing: **50 more items are waiting for your review → open your Needs-you inbox** (after one headline item).

This is not merely inconsistent copy. It sends the owner to an inbox that truthfully contains zero owner decisions and dumps a long list of technical coworker/platform items into the opening message.

## Evidence and verified cause

Observed on the development consumer install at `/workspace` (release `v2026.08.23-cycle4.1`; screenshot supplied by operator).

Live state:
- `WorkItem`: 1 queued item, unassigned to a human.
- `Agent`: 99 active coworker records.
- Workspace renders 0 owner items and 51 digital-team-handled items.

Deployed source:
- `components/workspace-home/OperatorCockpit.tsx` calls `buildOwnerAttentionProjection(visible, ...)` and displays `projection.count`, which is `needsYouNow.length`.
- `lib/agent/opening-briefing-loader.ts` passes the raw operator-visible `AttentionItem[]` directly to `composeOpeningBriefing`.
- `lib/agent/opening-briefing.ts` calculates `remaining = input.items.length - 1` and labels every remaining raw item “waiting for your review.”

Thus 51 custodian/digest items correctly demoted by Workspace are incorrectly relabeled by the coworker as 1 headline plus 50 owner-review items.

## Scope

In:
- Make the coworker opening briefing use the same owner-routing projection as Workspace and the Needs-you inbox.
- Keep proactive briefing behavior, counts, links, and copy honest for `needs-you-now`, `weekly-digest`, and `custodian` lanes.
- Add regression coverage for a fresh-install attention feed dominated by technical/provider/platform items.
- Refactor the shared projection seam so these two surfaces cannot drift again; allocate roughly 20% of implementation effort to removing duplicated/divergent classification logic.

Out:
- Changing attention-source adapters or suppressing legitimate technical work.
- Redesigning the entire coworker panel.
- Editing installed runtime assets directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `needsYouNow.length === 0` and 51 custodian/digest items, a balanced coworker does **not** claim anything is waiting for the owner’s review and does not link to the Needs-you inbox as if it contains work.
- With one genuine `needs-you-now` item plus team-held items, the briefing headlines/counts only genuine owner decisions; team-held work may be summarized separately with explicit “your digital team is handling this” language.
- The coworker briefing, `/workspace`, and `/workspace/inbox` derive owner counts from one shared projection contract.
- The opening bubble does not render an unbounded comma-separated list of technical coworker names on a fresh install.
- Unit coverage reproduces the exact contradiction: 51 raw items, 0 owner decisions, and verifies the false “50 more … waiting for your review” copy is absent.
- Functional verification on a fresh local install observes: Workspace count 0; coworker either stays silent at balanced proactivity or gives an honest all-clear at assertive proactivity; destination inbox also shows 0.
- Existing behavior for genuine approvals/escalations remains intact.

## UX fit review

- Decision: fits-with-guardrails.
- Owning area: Workspace.

items.title: dpf_state_lock_acquire returns 1 silently on its reclaim-wait deadline while the sibling deadline reports install_state_lock_timeout
items.body:
CORRECTED 2026-08-26. The original body of this item was wrong on two counts and is replaced.

WHAT I GOT WRONG (recorded so nobody re-chases it):
- I claimed `dpf_state_validate_file() { node ... >/dev/null; }` swallowed the validator's explanation. It does NOT. The validator writes failures with console.error, i.e. stderr, and `>/dev/null` discards stdout only. Verified empirically: running it exactly as the function does still prints `install-state invalid: $: malformed_json`.
- I claimed the 2026-08-16 E2E silent abort was unexplained and outstanding. It was root-caused and FIXED by PR #4367, "fix(install): unbreak every fresh Linux/macOS install (unmatched glob under set -e)". Cause: dpf_state_cleanup_temps had no nullglob, so on a fresh install the unmatched glob stayed literal, `[ -f ]` was false, and that false test was the loop's last command — making the function return 1 under `set -e` with no message. A regression test ships at scripts/installer/lib/state-cleanup-temps.test.mjs (5/5 passing, registered in the CI inventory in scripts/lib/ci-policy-guards.mjs).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY STILL BROKEN (verified on origin/main 79f0b1c7):

scripts/installer/lib/state.sh, dpf_state_lock_acquire has two 30-second deadline paths and only one of them speaks:

  L88   if dpf_state_active_reclaim_first "$lock" >/dev/null; then now="$(date +%s)"; [ "$now" -ge "$deadline" ] && return 1; sleep 0.05; continue; fi
  L119  [ "$now" -ge "$deadline" ] && { echo "install_state_lock_timeout" >&2; return 1; }

Same function, same budget, same meaning — the caller gave up waiting for the install-state lock. L119 emits `install_state_lock_timeout`; L88 returns 1 with nothing. dpf_state_init consumes it as `dpf_state_lock_acquire "$path" || return 1`, and install-dpf.sh calls dpf_state_init bare under `set -euo pipefail`. So if an install loses that particular race it hangs ~30s and then aborts with a bare exit 1 — the same undiagnosable shape #4367 just fixed, on a neighbouring path.

Deliberately NOT in scope (checked and correct as-is):
- L81 `return 1` in dpf_state_active_reclaim_first is a normal "no active reclaim ticket found" negative result, not an error. Must stay silent.
- dpf_platform / dpf_arch already print their own diagnostics before returning 1.
- The commit-candidate wrappers (L227/L284/L300/L367/L380) look bare but their callees (node validator, mv, python3 flush) all write to stderr themselves.

FIX: emit a timeout marker on the L88 path, distinguishable from L119 so the two races are tellable apart, and make the 30s budget overridable so the path is testable in under a second rather than only by a 30-second wall clock. Add a regression test alongside the existing state.sh bash-driven suite.

items.title: Estate Discovery is unreachable on a fresh install: discovery_sweep is vetoed by a constitutional alignment gate demanding six GTM criteria that onboarding never collects
items.body:
## What happens

On a cycle-4 install that completed onboarding **11/11**, calling `discovery_sweep` is refused:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "discovery_sweep rejected: Constitutional alignment could not be established
              from complete criteria and all required corpora; escalating rather than
              inventing fit.",
  "error": "alignment_escalation_required",
  "data": { "interactionId": "DI-2B3156C625AD",
    "alignment": { "verdict": "escalate",
      "criteria": { "market": null, "segment": null, "product": null,
                    "motion": null, "geography": null, "customerType": null },
      "evidence": [], "missing": ["market","segment","product","motion",
                                  "geography","customerType"] } } }
```

All six criteria are null, and **no onboarding step collects any of them.** The eleven steps are
account, business context, AI providers, branding, how-you-decide, operating hours, storefront,
platform dev, build, meet-your-COO, workspace. None asks for market, segment, motion, geography
or customer type.

So the gate is unsatisfiable through the product's own setup path. There is no operator-facing
message anywhere explaining this — the failure only appears if you call the tool directly. The
`Run Sweep` button on `/platform/tools/discovery` presumably hits the same veto.

## Why this matters more than a blocked button

The refusal itself is **correct behaviour** and I want to be clear about that: refusing to
invent a fit rather than guessing is exactly right, and it produced a proper ledger id
(`DI-2B3156C625AD`). The defect is that the gate's inputs have no supply. A guard that can
never be satisfied is indistinguishable from a broken feature.

## The second half: discovery already ran anyway

`summarize_estate_posture` reports a completed run — so something *is* sweeping:

| Run | Source | Trigger | Items |
|---|---|---|---|
| DISC-1787530206293 | `dpf_bootstrap` | scheduled | 17 |
| DISC-1787526606345 | `dpf_bootstrap` | scheduled | 17 |

Hourly since install, with **zero configured connections**
(`list_discovery_connections` -> `0 discovery connection(s)`).

The scheduled bootstrap sweep is not subject to the alignment gate; the operator-initiated one
is. **The guard applies to the human and not to the machine**, which is backwards — the
scheduled path has no operator present to escalate to.

## What it discovered: DPF's own Docker internals

All 17 entities are the install itself — containers (`dpf-portal-1`, `dpf-postgres-1`,
`dpf-redis-1`, `dpf-inngest-1`), the Docker host, the Docker runtime, its bridge subnets
(`172.17.0.0/16`, `172.18.0.0/16`) and gateways.

Three are flagged `attributionStatus = needs_review` at confidence 0.6:

```
host | LAN Host 172.18.0.1 | needs_review | 0.6
host | LAN Host 172.18.0.2 | needs_review | 0.6
host | LAN Host 172.18.0.5 | needs_review | 0.6
```

Those are **Docker's own `dpf_default` bridge addresses** — the very containers discovery
attributed correctly two rows earlier. The same run identifies `dpf-postgres-1` at confidence
0.9 and then re-reports its bridge IP as an unidentified LAN host needing human review.

`summarize_estate_posture` surfaces this as `3 items need review` plus
`gateway_connection_needed: 3` and `taxonomy_attribution_low_confidence: 3`. A non-technical
operator on day one sees nine posture issues on an estate consisting entirely of DPF talking to
itself, with no way to know they are self-inflicted.

**Suggested fix:** attribute container-network addresses against the containers already
identified in the same run, and suppress `needs_review` for addresses inside a Docker bridge
subnet the run itself enumerated.

## Positive — identity resolution is genuinely correct

Worth recording because it is the hard part and it works. Two independent runs produced 34
`DiscoveredItem` observations that resolved to exactly **17 distinct `inventoryEntityId`
values** from 17 distinct `observedKey`s. Nothing duplicated, nothing drifted. The
observation-per-run + canonical-entity split is the right shape.

## Open question, not asserted as a defect

Observations accumulate per run: 17 items + 20 relationships each, hourly, retained. No
retention or prune is visible in the schema. At that cadence an idle install discovering only
itself writes roughly 150k item rows and 175k relationship rows per year. Worth confirming a
prune exists before that is a problem on a long-lived install.

## Found by

Dogfood reset cycle 4, Phase 5 (estate discovery), on a fresh install with onboarding at 11/11.
Related: BI-EFC3C31D (onboarding never touches estate discovery).

---

## UPDATE 2026-08-24 — verified with a live UniFi gateway connected

The operator connected a real gateway and ran it. Three things are now settled.

### 1. The veto is independent of gateway connectivity

Connection state at the time of retest:

```json
{ "connectionKey": "unifi:192.168.0.1", "name": "Network Gateway",
  "status": "active", "hasApiKey": true,
  "lastTestStatus": "ok", "lastTestMessage": "Discovered 75 items" }
```

`discovery_sweep` was rejected again, identically, new ledger id **DI-4220D47E2459**, all six
criteria still null. Connecting a gateway does not and cannot satisfy the alignment gate —
the two are unrelated. The operator-initiated refresh path is blocked permanently, on every
install, regardless of configuration.

### 2. Discovery is reachable only through the Save & Test side door

The connection test performed a **real discovery run and persisted it**: run key
`unifi:192.168.0.1:e67f024d-...`, 75 items, 70 relationships, status `completed`.

So the write path is not gated at all, and the refresh path is gated impassably. There are now
three ways discovery data enters this install — the scheduled `dpf_bootstrap` sweep, the
connection test — and the one the operator is meant to use is the only one that fails.
`Save & Test` is load-bearing by accident: it is the sole operator-reachable way to refresh the
estate, which means the only way to re-scan is to re-test the connection.

### 3. `gateway_connection_needed: 3` cannot ever clear — it points at Docker

This is the sharpest part. After connecting the gateway, posture still reports:

```
gateway_connection_needed        3
attribution_missing              3
taxonomy_attribution_low_confidence  3
```

Every `needs_review` observation in the database — 9 rows, 3 entities — comes from
`sourceSlug=dpf_bootstrap`, and all three are Docker bridge addresses:

```
host | LAN Host 172.18.0.1 | dpf_bootstrap | conf=0.6
host | LAN Host 172.18.0.2 | dpf_bootstrap | conf=0.6
host | LAN Host 172.18.0.5 | dpf_bootstrap | conf=0.6
```

**Zero came from the real network.** No gateway will ever explain `172.18.0.x` — they are this
install's own containers. So the product tells the operator to connect a gateway to resolve
three issues that a gateway is structurally incapable of resolving. The operator does it,
the count stays at 3, and there is no path forward from the posture surface.

### The collector itself is good — record this as a positive

The UniFi run attributed **better than DPF's own self-discovery**:

| Type | Count | needs_review | avg confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| network_client | 68 | 0 | 0.80 |
| access_point | 4 | 0 | 0.95 |
| router | 1 | 0 | 0.95 |
| switch | 1 | 0 | 0.95 |
| wan_uplink | 1 | 0 | 0.95 |

75 real devices, **zero needing review**, sensible vendor/model naming from MAC OUI and UniFi
metadata, and operator-assigned names carried through intact. The one number that rose was
`catalog_match_ambiguous` (1 -> 8), which is honest: real hardware now needs real catalog
matching.

The defect is entirely in the gate and the self-discovery attribution, not in the collector.

### Revised fixes

1. Give the alignment criteria a supply, or exempt read-only estate discovery from the GTM
   alignment gate. As shipped it can never be satisfied.
2. Apply the same gate to the scheduled `dpf_bootstrap` sweep and the connection test, or to
   neither. Guarding only the attended path is backwards.
3. Attribute container-network addresses against the containers identified in the same run,
   and never raise `gateway_connection_needed` for an address inside a Docker bridge subnet
   the run itself enumerated.

items.title: Preserve initiative organization authority through external reviewer approval replay
items.body:
## Problem

A commit-bound external initiative reviewer can create and receive human approval for `record_initiative_evidence`, but the approved replay writes `AuthorizationDecisionLog.organizationId = null` even when the governed backlog item belongs to an organization. The receipt repository correctly rejects the write with `Reviewer authority does not match the initiative organization`, leaving readiness permanently blocked.

## Evidence

Task `TR-MCP-Y210Nmg3bjg3MDBnYTAxbXhheDU2MXV2aQ-81B91B05D72C` targeted `BI-MCP-EFF-0285909C` at immutable commit `a08cf14638a5ee4445ddaa43beebff30f88500d2`. Its envelope was approved, then exact idempotent replay reached the writer and failed. The backlog item organization is `ORG-1787529949989` (`rescue`); both the require-approval and allow authority decisions had a null organization.

## Scope

Propagate the governed initiative organization into the external reviewer TaskRun authority context and both the approval-envelope and approved-replay decisions. Preserve immutable binding, idempotency, independent-reviewer identity, and tenant isolation. Do not weaken receipt-repository organization checks or introduce an override.

## Acceptance criteria

- The initial bound reviewer tool call records a require-approval decision with the initiative organization.
- Exact replay after employee approval records an allow decision with the same organization and executes the writer once.
- A mismatched organization remains denied.
- Idempotent replay cannot change organization, artifact, reviewer, gate, or input identity.
- Tests cover organization-bound, platform-null, mismatch, and approval-resume paths.

Blocks: BI-MCP-EFF-0285909C and all organization-bound initiatives using external readiness reviewers.

Discovered while delivering the resilient gate-flow control program.

items.title: The operator inbox renders 24 distinct coworker tasks as 24 byte-identical rows: the attention projection carries each title but the card discards it, and every one of them recommends keeping the work with a specialist
items.body:
## What the operator sees

`/workspace/inbox`, headed:

> **What needs you now** — "Business choices only, written in plain language. Your digital team
> keeps technical recovery and low-urgency review out of today's count."
>
> **28 things need you today**

Of those 28, **24 are byte-identical**:

> **Help your coworker continue?** · Reversible
> A coworker paused and needs your input to continue.
> IF YOU DO NOTHING — your coworker stays stuck here and the work behind it waits.
> AI RECOMMENDATION — Digital workforce — Keep this with the specialist unless it forces a
> business choice from you.

There are only four distinct question types across the whole inbox: *Help your coworker
continue?*, *Approve this coworker action?*, *How should we fix this for customers?*, *Make this
business decision?*

## The underlying data is NOT identical

24 `TaskRun` rows in `input-required` with **23 distinct titles**:

```
Canonical-digest Vitest timeout research review
Independent spec approval of compact complete local-CI Vitest timeout design
Independently review immutable BI-F3422349 design and persist the spec-approval ...
Independently approve or reject the immutable bounded exhaustive-Vitest terminat...
Render one governed decision on the compact immutable bounded exhaustive-Vitest ...
Independent Vitest timeout research review
```

And the projection already carries it — `apps/web/lib/attention/sources/paused-ai.ts:72`:

```ts
return {
  id: `paused-ai:${row.taskRunId}`,
  source: "paused-ai",
  title: row.title,          // <- distinguishing information, present
  context: readSummary(row.progressPayload)
    ?? "A coworker paused and needs your input to continue.",
  ...
```

**This is a rendering defect, not a data defect.** The card shows the generic question and the
generic fallback `context`, and drops `title` entirely. Every item also falls back on `context`
because `readSummary(progressPayload)` returns null for these runs, so the one field that could
have differentiated them is empty too.

## Three separate problems, worth separating

**1. The list is unusable.** Twenty-four identical rows cannot be triaged, prioritised, or even
counted meaningfully. An operator cannot tell whether they are looking at one problem shown 24
times or 24 problems. Nothing indicates which coworker, which work, or which decision.

**2. The surface contradicts itself.** The page says "Business choices only... your digital team
keeps technical recovery out of today's count", and then every one of the 24 carries
**"Keep this with the specialist unless it forces a business choice from you."** The system's own
recommendation on all 24 is *not yours* — while counting them in "28 things need you today". If
the recommendation is trustworthy, they should not be in the count; if they belong in the count,
the recommendation is wrong. Both cannot hold.

**3. None of it is this business.** The organization here is a pet rescue. All 24 titles are
platform-engineering tasks — Vitest timeout research, spec approvals, canonical-digest reviews.
A shelter operator opening "what needs you now" is shown two dozen requests to approve CI test
infrastructure decisions.

## Suggested fix

Ordered by value:

1. **Render `title`.** It is already on the item. The generic question can stay as a category
   label, but the title must be the heading — otherwise the projection's work is thrown away at
   the last step.
2. **Collapse or group identical-shaped items.** Twenty-four paused coworkers is one situation,
   not 24 decisions; a grouped row with a count and an expander respects the operator's
   attention.
3. **Honour the AI recommendation in the count.** An item whose recommendation is "keep this with
   the specialist" should not be in "things need you today" unless the operator asks to see
   specialist-held work. This is the difference between an inbox and a log.
4. **Populate `context`.** `readSummary(progressPayload)` returns null for every one of these
   runs, so the fallback is doing all the work. Either the runs should write a progress summary
   or the fallback should synthesise from the title.

## Standing UX requirement this violates

From `docs/architecture/archetypes/pet-rescue-operating-model.md` §7: *to the point for the
intended activity, minimal cognitive overload, no erroneous distractions for day-to-day
workers.* An inbox of 24 indistinguishable platform-engineering prompts is the clearest failure
of that requirement found so far, and it sits on the operator's primary surface.

Related: `BI-7A38F667` (workspace answers commercial questions on a shelter). Found during
dogfood reset cycle 4.

items.title: Coworker thread repeats role identity and exposes voice controls that runtime cannot fulfill
items.body:
## Problem

The coworker decision thread repeats the named coworker and role above every assistant turn even though the panel header already establishes identity. The same composer presents ambiguous speaker controls without distinguishing user preference from TTS/STT runtime capability, so a missing synthesis service looks like an unexplained disabled or ineffective control.

## Scope

In:
- establish a clear identity hierarchy: conversational name as the primary label and role as secondary context once per thread/panel;
- remove redundant full name-plus-role repetition from consecutive assistant messages while preserving accessible authorship;
- derive voice-control availability from existing profile preference, voice-profile readiness, and live TTS/STT service health;
- represent playback and dictation as separate capabilities with truthful labels, pressed state, disabled reasons, and recovery guidance;
- prevent transient connection state from masquerading as permanent voice disablement;
- refactor duplicated identity/voice-state derivation into shared typed view models (target about 20% of implementation effort).

Out:
- changing the coworker’s canonical identity, authority, permissions, or audit records;
- redesigning the whole coworker panel;
- implementing or replacing the TTS engine;
- the unrelated attention-labeling behavior owned by BI-2C50F548.

## Acceptance criteria

- The panel establishes the coworker’s conversational name and role without repeating the full combined label above every assistant response.
- Screen readers retain unambiguous authorship for each assistant message.
- Playback availability combines voice preference, ready voice profile, and current synthesis-service health; an unavailable service has an explicit reason.
- Dictation health and playback health are evaluated and presented independently.
- Mute/unmute labels and aria-pressed semantics describe the current action/state consistently.
- Connecting state is visually and semantically distinct from unsupported, disabled-by-preference, and service-unavailable states.
- Regression tests cover identity repetition, TTS unavailable, STT available/TTS unavailable, preference disabled, and connecting states.
- The affected coworker thread is verified in the running portal in light and dark themes, including keyboard and accessible-name behavior.

items.title: Teardown clears the model store, so every reset cycle re-downloads ~20 GB, and partial pulls leave stub entries
items.body:
A zero-footprint teardown removes the Docker Model Runner store along with everything else, so step 8 of the next install re-downloads the entire local model.

Measured on cycle 4: a ~20 GB pull, the single longest step in the reset loop.

## Why it matters now

The reset cycle is meant to be repeated often, and by more than one tester. A 20 GB download per cycle is the main thing that will stop people running it. This is worth an explicit decision rather than an accident of the teardown being thorough.

- If retaining the model between cycles is acceptable, the teardown should say it is keeping it and why, so the next tester is not surprised by a fast install and does not assume the model store is stale.
- If removal is intended, the documented cost belongs in the playbook up front so testers budget for it.

## Two defects observed alongside it

**The progress counter exceeds 100%.** Cycle 4 logged `Downloaded 31.95GB of 19.91GB` -- monotonically increasing, no restart, final model 17.66 GiB. Roughly double-counted. While it is wrong, an operator cannot distinguish a slow download from a stuck one, which is exactly when they most need the indicator.

**Partial pulls leave stub entries that look like installed models.** `docker model ls` showed:

```
qwen3-coder    (no parameters, no quantization, no architecture, no size)    56 years ago
```

`docker model inspect` confirms `"created": 0` and a config containing only `{"format": "gguf"}`. The 1970-epoch timestamp renders as "56 years ago". A reader scanning the model list sees a model that is not there, and tooling that checks presence by name would find it.

Related: the model registers under a different name than it is pulled by -- pulled as `hf.co/ggml-org/...`, registered as `huggingface.co/ggml-org/...` -- which the installer comments predict and which is a plausible source of these stubs.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 4, image v2026.08.23-cycle4.1.

items.title: Self-upgrade is blocked on a consumer release install by capability_state_stale
items.body:
A consumer release install (D:\\DPF, environmentClass development) cannot self-upgrade. Every governed run fails in the promoter capability preflight with `error: capability_state_stale`, so the instance had to be moved onto a new release out-of-band (DPF_IMAGE_TAG bump plus compose recreate).

Evidence from run SUR / SelfUpgradeRun rows on 2026-08-23:
1. First failure was `promoter-unavailable`: PlatformConfig self_upgrade sets promoterImage to the bare name `dpf-promoter`, so `docker run` resolved it against Docker Hub and got `pull access denied`. The image IS published to GHCR at every release tag. Providing a local `dpf-promoter:latest` alias got past this.
2. Second and third failures were `capability_state_stale`, with the promoter image matched to the running portal version, ruling out promoter/launcher version skew.

Root cause evidence: `resolveCapabilityServiceProjection` in scripts/lib/capability-service-projection.mjs throws capability_state_stale when the live active capability set differs from install-state.enabledRuntimeCapabilities. On this install PlatformCapability has SEVEN active rows (runtime:core, runtime:build, runtime:browser-automation, runtime:deep-observability, runtime:durable-automation, runtime:external-ai, runtime:local-speech) while install-state.json records only [\"runtime:core\"]. Capabilities were activated in the portal without install-state being restamped.

scripts/installer/migrate-install-state.mjs restamps hashes when the CATALOG moves; it does not reconcile install-state to the databases active capability set, so it does not repair this drift.

Notes: the /dpf-state mount was verified working (the Windows host path mounts fine and install-state.json is readable inside a container), so this is not the #3262 mounts-denied class. DPF_STATE_DIR_HOST is set correctly on the portal.

Suggested fix: make capability activation write through to install-state, or give the promoter preflight a governed reconcile path that restamps enabledRuntimeCapabilities from the live set instead of failing closed.

THREE SOURCES OF TRUTH, THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS, on this install right now:

| Capability | install-state.json | PlatformCapability.state | Containers actually running |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| runtime:core | enabled | active | portal, postgres — yes |
| runtime:build | NOT enabled | active | sandbox, sandbox-postgres — RUNNING |
| runtime:durable-automation | NOT enabled | active | redis, inngest — RUNNING |
| runtime:deep-observability | NOT enabled | **active** | **NONE** — no prometheus, grafana, loki, alloy, postgres-exporter |
| runtime:browser-automation | NOT enabled | active | browser-use — NOT running |
| runtime:local-speech | NOT enabled | active | dpf-stt, dpf-tts — NOT running |
| runtime:external-ai | NOT enabled | active | n/a on this host |
| runtime:development | NOT enabled | **disabled** | dev-portal, dev-postgres — **RUNNING** |

`install-state.json` reports `enabledRuntimeCapabilities: ["runtime:core"]` and nothing else. The database reports seven capabilities `active`. The running topology agrees with the database for build and durable-automation, contradicts it for deep-observability, browser-automation and local-speech, and INVERTS it for development (disabled in the database, running on the host).

WHY THIS SHOULD BE IMPOSSIBLE: per `docs/architecture/capability-driven-runtime-profiles.md`, a transition "commits live capability state only after the signed host receipt proves the exact topology and required health", and `OperationalCapabilityState` joins the catalog projection, install-state, live database state and bounded Docker observations. A three-way divergence means either a path wrote capability state without a host receipt, or the reinstall on 2026-08-24 rewrote install-state without reconciling the database rows, or reconciliation runs but does not report disagreement.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is not cosmetic:
1. **Observability is silently absent.** `runtime:deep-observability` reads `active`, so any surface trusting capability state believes Prometheus, Grafana, Loki and Alloy are collecting. Nothing is. Every metric-backed panel, alert and health signal that depends on them has no source, and the state that would reveal it says everything is fine.
2. **Backup, diagnostics, readiness and the health UI all consume `OperationalCapabilityState`.** If it cannot see this divergence, none of them can.
3. It made the Edge Node gap in BI-6052C2C2 harder to diagnose, because capability state could not be trusted as evidence of what is actually deployed.

`docs/architecture/platform-overview.md:406` compounds it by stating "The headless monitoring stack (Prometheus, Loki, Alloy, and the metric exporters) runs as part of the default Docker Compose stack". That is FALSE against the current compose file: all four sit behind the `runtime-deep-observability` profile and start only on capability activation. Grafana's opt-in status is documented correctly two lines earlier, which makes the wrong half more credible.

SCOPE:
1. Determine which writer can move `PlatformCapability.state` without a host receipt, and close it.
2. Make `OperationalCapabilityState` REPORT divergence rather than absorb it — a capability whose services are absent is a finding, not a rounding error. Surface it on the runtime-health page.
3. Reconcile this install: either start the deep-observability closure or correct the state to match reality. Do not simply flip the database rows; whatever did that once will do it again.
4. Fix `platform-overview.md:406`.
5. Decide whether `runtime:development` running while marked disabled is a separate defect or the same one seen from the other side.

EVIDENCE: `install-state.json` `enabledRuntimeCapabilities: ["runtime:core"]`, `capabilityCatalogHash c83c56c0e3602293ee01abd1d5f068380d23de3244b4d2a05b06f26a12ce3cb9`; `select "capabilityId", state from "PlatformCapability"`; `docker compose ps -a`.

items.title: verify_live_install_readiness returns BLOCKED on every consumer install because the portal container has no git to compute ancestry
items.body:
## Observed

Filed on the explicit instruction of the tool's own `nextAction: { kind: "file-blocker-bi" }`.

`verify_live_install_readiness` with a real merged feature commit returns:

```json
{"verdict":"BLOCKED",
 "reason":"Cannot determine whether served bytes (c851313fc708) contain feature commit aa456254b6ab — ancestry was not computable.",
 "served":{"sha":"c851313fc7082ef9ebdb6334906f4bca8f76f07f","source":"git-sha"},
 "feature":{"sha":"aa456254b6ab2b37596cd394ccacb11b715f079a"},
 "nextAction":{"kind":"file-blocker-bi",
   "detail":"No git repository found at process.cwd() or DPF_REPO_ROOT. Point DPF_REPO_ROOT at the DPF clone (or mount .git into the portal) so ancestry can be computed."}}
```

Both SHAs are correct and present. Only the ancestry computation fails.

## Why this matters more than a missing convenience

The tool's contract is a three-way verdict: `CAN-TEST` (served bytes contain the feature), `MUST-ADVANCE` (behind → advance via governed self-upgrade), or `BLOCKED` (no testable runtime → file a BI and stop). `BLOCKED` is the "stop working" verdict.

On a consumer install the portal container has no `.git` and `DPF_REPO_ROOT` is unset, so ancestry is never computable and the answer is **always** `BLOCKED` — including in the common, healthy case where the truthful answer is `MUST-ADVANCE` (advance the install and carry on). The verdict that means "give up and escalate" is returned for the situation that needs no escalation at all.

The correct verdict for the case above was `MUST-ADVANCE`. Computed by hand from the source clone at `D:\DPF-source-root`:

```
git rev-list --count c851313fc708..origin/main   → 11
git merge-base --is-ancestor aa456254b6 c851313fc708  → false
```

The running image is 11 commits behind `main` and does not contain the feature. That is an ordinary "advance the install" situation.

This is the consumer-install shape of the same class as `BI-89887875` (self-upgrade assuming a Git checkout in a release install) and `BI-5AA89F68` (preflight requiring a source-only capability adapter): a source-oriented mechanism reached for on an install that deliberately holds no source.

## Directions worth weighing, not prescribed

Ancestry between two commits does not require a local clone. Options include asking the provider (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{base}...{head}` returns `status: behind|ahead|identical|diverged`, which answers this directly), reading a recorded lineage the release artifact already carries, or honouring `DPF_REPO_ROOT` when an operator has a clone available. Whichever is chosen, an install with no source must still be able to reach `CAN-TEST` and `MUST-ADVANCE`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a consumer install with no `.git` and no `DPF_REPO_ROOT`, a feature commit that is absent from the served image returns `MUST-ADVANCE`, not `BLOCKED`.
2. A feature commit contained in the served image returns `CAN-TEST` on the same install.
3. `BLOCKED` is reserved for a genuinely untestable runtime — no served identity at all — and no longer fires merely because ancestry could not be computed locally.
4. When ancestry cannot be established by any available means, the verdict states which input was missing and names an attainable next action for a source-free install.
5. Regression test uses a source-free fixture (no `.git`, no `DPF_REPO_ROOT`) and asserts all three verdicts.
6. Contributor installs with a reachable clone keep their current behaviour.

Provenance: hit while confirming whether the `BI-A8BFEFCE` fix had reached the running install, 2026-08-26. Running image `v2026.08.25-consumer-self-upgrade.2`, revision `c851313fc708`.

items.title: The 24 GB VRAM tier selects a vision model over a coder, and the code comments say it is the wrong choice
items.body:
**Operator has raised this more than once.** Recording it with the evidence so the decision can be made deliberately rather than rediscovered each cycle.

## The ladder is coder -> vision -> coder

`install-dpf.ps1`:

```powershell
if     ($gpuVRAM_GB -ge 53) { "ai/qwen3-coder-next" }              # 80B MoE  -- coder
elseif ($gpuVRAM_GB -ge 23) { "hf.co/.../Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:Q4_K_M" } # dense, vision
elseif ($gpuVRAM_GB -ge 21) { "ai/qwen3-coder" }                    # 30B MoE  -- coder
```

A 24 GB card lands on the one rung that is not a coding model. **A card with LESS VRAM (21-22 GB) gets a coder.** Selection is non-monotonic in capability for this platform's actual local work.

## The code's own comments contradict the behaviour

Both `local-model-policy.ts` (LOCAL_MODEL_TIERS) and `scripts/detect-hardware-host.ts` (SELECTION_TIERS) annotate the tier below as:

```
{ model: "ai/qwen3-coder", weightsGb: 16 },  // the 24 GB-card sweet spot (measured ~20.7 GB @ 24k ctx)
```

So the codebase calls `ai/qwen3-coder` the 24 GB sweet spot, while 24 GB cards are routed past it.

## But the placement was deliberate, and that deserves weighing

```
// That trade is deliberate: the operator criterion for the local tier is a
// thorough, trustworthy result rather than time-to-answer (2026-08-16).
//
// Ranked ABOVE the 30B coder despite being the newer/smaller-footprint model
// because the ladder is "largest that fits" and quality here does not track size.
```

That rationale optimises general reasoning. What has since become clear is how badly it collides with the rest of the platform:

- Build Studio requires a **code-capable runner** and declines this model.
- The code-gen route excludes `local` (compounded by the unreviewed-evidence defect).
- The same file admits the vision benefit is not even delivered: *"It does NOT yet resolve as vision-capable despite being a native VLM -- see BI-C2EFF855."*
- It is the only tier pulled from HuggingFace rather than the curated `ai/` namespace, and on cycle 4 the pinned digest **did not match** because upstream republished.
- It is DENSE, so ~4x slower per turn than the MoE tiers either side.

Net: the 24 GB tier gets a slow model chosen for thoroughness, whose vision capability does not resolve, which the build path will not use, from the one namespace with a supply-chain incident this week.

## Cost per reset cycle

~20 GB download at install step 8 -- the longest single step -- for a model the codegen path cannot use.

## Decision needed

1. **Reverse the ranking** so 24 GB cards get `ai/qwen3-coder`. Matches what the comments already claim, and the MoE is faster.
2. **Make it conditional on install purpose** -- coder when the install will do platform development, thorough-dense otherwise. More faithful to the original reasoning, more work.

**Keep in sync:** the ladder is duplicated in `install-dpf.ps1`, `apps/web/lib/inference/local-model-policy.ts` (LOCAL_MODEL_TIERS) and `scripts/detect-hardware-host.ts` (SELECTION_TIERS), with a pinned `expectedDigest` in the installer and policy. A change must update all of them or the over-commit guard flags drift.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 4, operator-raised (repeat).

items.title: Restore flow efficiency across DPF external-agent delivery gates
items.body:
## Problem

The development host ran continuously for seven hours but produced only four PRs (about 0.57 PR/hour). Tasks accumulate behind scarce exact-tree CI, preview, and semantic-review gates while task-local Node runners repeatedly poll MCP. The measured lease tools produced 1,297 calls, with 1,222 estimated as waste. Pure documentation and affected-scope changes can still enter the same exhaustive local pipeline as schema or runtime changes, contrary to the canonical resilient-concurrent-development process.

## Scope

Update the existing resilient concurrent-development design and implement the missing flow-control slices:

- make the existing CI evidence plan authoritative before scarce capacity is claimed;
- coalesce identical immutable gate/review requests and reuse valid receipts;
- represent queued work as durable Workroom/TaskRun wait state and wake it through event adapters;
- govern every heavyweight local process through shared resource lanes;
- enforce WIP, progress SLOs, stale-wait escalation, and truthful Workroom liveness.

Do not create a parallel task bus, queue model, Workroom ledger, or agent memory. Reuse NonProductionEnvironmentLease, QueueTelemetryEvent, TaskRun, WorkroomActivity, Inngest, the agent event bus, MCP Tasks, and exact-tree stage receipts.

## Acceptance criteria

- Pure documentation changes complete their required local evidence without claiming the heavyweight local-integration-ci lease.
- Affected changes execute mapped tests and proportional package/build evidence; unknown or high-risk scope fails closed to exhaustive verification.
- One immutable gate identity executes at most once for a matching base tree, integration tree, policy digest, evidence-plan digest, and toolchain fingerprint.
- Queued tasks checkpoint and become dormant; normal admission does not require a live polling Node runner.
- A capacity event wakes the head waiter, which performs one fresh pressure-aware claim; a bounded reconciliation fallback repairs missed events.
- Heavy typecheck, exhaustive test, production build, preview, inference, and semantic-review workloads obey explicit resource-lane admission.
- Workrooms distinguish running, durable waiting, ready-to-resume, terminal, and stale; queued lease evidence prevents false reaping.
- Flow telemetry reports arrivals, WIP, wait, process, cycle time, throughput, first-pass yield, abandonment, duplicate suppression, and PR throughput.
- Baseline and target are explicit: improve from 4 PRs/7h while reducing wait-related MCP calls by at least 95%, with no weakened immutable-tree evidence.
- The program is decomposed into independently shippable BIs, one branch and PR per BI.

## Dependencies

Extends the existing 2026-08-15 resilient concurrent-development process, reusable queue telemetry, nonproduction lease, MCP Tasks, and Workroom convergence substrate. Decision DI-83C76A3C1B58 selected durable flow control with high confidence.

## Problem

The live platform exposes Stack Currency from a route-owned static `PLATFORM_STACK` array even though DigitalProduct, ProductDependency, InventoryEntity, BomDocument/BomComponent, CatalogIdentity, and lifecycle milestones already form the canonical portfolio and software-supply-chain substrate. The DPF Portal product currently has zero persisted BOM documents, and its Supply Chain content is hidden under a separate Operate sub-route, so operators see duplicated concepts and no usable SBOM.

Root cause evidence:
- PR #4295 added the static stack source after the SBOM substrate had shipped in PR #958 and the portfolio projector in PR #2269.
- PR #4295 recorded no independent review and its plan incorrectly asserted that stack assessment had no other consumer.
- The existing projector parity guard only covers registered projectors; it cannot detect a route-local competing read model.
- On the 2026-08-24 development install, BomDocument, BomComponent, and BomComponentOccurrence each contain zero rows; `prov-azure-openai` also has zero inventory and BOM rows.
- Kernel consultation DI-C24852C1789A selected the product-Operate canonical option with high confidence and autonomy eligibility.

## Scope

In:
- Make the DPF Portal DigitalProduct Operate area the one operator home for product dependencies, discovered estate, software composition/SBOM, and component currency.
- Reuse the existing CycloneDX platform generator and persist its result through the canonical BomDocument/BomComponent/CatalogIdentity substrate for `dpf-portal`.
- Derive component currency from CatalogIdentity lifecycle milestones through the canonical lifecycle helper.
- Remove the static platform-stack data owner and redirect the legacy Stack Currency route to the canonical product Operate destination.
- Add an architectural invariant that fails if a route-owned platform stack inventory is reintroduced.
- Improve navigation and empty states so SBOM/currency are visible without knowing a hidden sub-route exists.

Out:
- Collapsing the broader `dpf-meta` versus `dpf-portal` product-identity debt.
- Treating long-tail libraries as standalone DigitalProducts.
- Replacing CycloneDX or the release-container attestation mechanism.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] There is exactly one persisted platform software-composition source: the generated CycloneDX BOM linked to the `dpf-portal` DigitalProduct.
- [ ] Product Operate presents ProductDependency, InventoryEntity, BomDocument/BomComponent, and currency as distinct facets of one legible dependency surface.
- [ ] Component currency comes from CatalogIdentity lifecycle milestones; the UI does not own support/EOL dates.
- [ ] The legacy `/ops/stack-currency` URL redirects to the canonical product Operate surface and no Stack Currency navigation tab remains.
- [ ] The static `PLATFORM_STACK` array and its route-owned source contract are removed.
- [ ] A fresh install/upgrade path idempotently persists the platform BOM; reruns replace/supersede rather than duplicate it.
- [ ] A regression guard prevents reintroduction of a route-local curated platform stack inventory.
- [ ] Tests cover persistence idempotence, lifecycle derivation, route redirect, unified surface states, and the architectural invariant.
- [ ] UI verification confirms first-viewport discoverability, responsive layout, empty/error behavior, and no duplicate navigation.

## Dependencies

Independent within EP-56AE0F69. Uses the already-shipped BomDocument/CatalogIdentity schema and platform SBOM generator.

items.title: The minimum attachment floor punches through the measured local tool ceiling, re-opening the fallback disqualification for any model measured below 12
items.body:
## Observed

`BI-A8BFEFCE` established the invariant that the attachment budget must never hand the model more tools than the routing gate will agree to run locally, and closed two paths that broke it. A third path is still open and shipped.

`deriveCoworkerToolCap` ends with:

```ts
return Math.max(MIN_COWORKER_ATTACHED_TOOLS, Math.min(ceiling, fitted));
```

The `MIN` floor is applied AFTER the ceiling, so it overrides it. Whenever a measured tool-fidelity ceiling is below `MIN_COWORKER_ATTACHED_TOOLS` (12), the budget attaches 12 while `callWithFallbackChain` refuses anything above the measured value. The unreadable-window branch has the same shape: `return Math.max(MIN, ceiling)`.

Exhaustively checked over windows `[null, 0, 4096, 16000, 24576, 32768, 131072, 262144]`, measured ceilings `[null, 4, 8, 10, 12, 15, 30, 48, 200]` and presences `[present, unknown]`: **48 combinations violate the invariant.** Examples:

```
window=null   measured=4   presence=present  -> cap=12 but gate=4
window=0      measured=8   presence=unknown  -> cap=12 but gate=8
window=24576  measured=10  presence=present  -> cap=12 but gate=10
```

## Why it matters

This is the original defect's failure mode, reinstated by a different route. The budget attaches 12 tools, the gate refuses the local endpoint for exceeding a limit of 4/8/10, and a cloud outage on top of it produces a turn that executes nothing — exactly the reviewer symptom `BI-A8BFEFCE` was raised for.

It is currently latent because no install has measured fidelity yet, so every ceiling resolves to the fail-safe cliff of 15 which sits above the floor. It arms the moment the Phase-2 eval harness measures any local model below 12 — and a weak small local model measuring 8 or 10 is exactly the case the harness exists to detect. The harness would then make the platform worse, silently.

## Cause

Operator precedence. `Math.max(MIN, Math.min(ceiling, fitted))` treats the floor as final. The floor's documented purpose is to stop WINDOW-fit arithmetic shrinking a coworker into uselessness on a small context — it was never meant to override evidence about what the model can actually select from. A measured ceiling is evidence; the floor is a guard against a different failure.

## Fix

Apply the floor to the window-fit term only, then bound by the ceiling:

```ts
if (!hasWindow) return ceiling;
return Math.min(ceiling, Math.max(MIN_COWORKER_ATTACHED_TOOLS, fitted));
```

Verified: 0 violations across the same matrix, and all nine documented behaviours unchanged (`131_072 → 15`, `131_072 + measured 40 → 40`, `24_576 → 15`, `16_000 → 12`, `4_096 → 12`, `1_000 → 12`, `null + absent → 48`, `null + unknown → 15`, `null + present → 15`).

The consequence to state plainly in the code: when a model measures below 12, the cap follows the measurement rather than the floor. Attaching more than the model has proven it can select from is not a kindness — the gate refuses it anyway, so the coworker gets nothing instead of a small working surface.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For every combination where a local model is in the serving path (`present` or `unknown`), `deriveCoworkerToolCap(...) <= resolveLocalToolCeiling(measured)`. Asserted as a matrix, not a sample.
2. The nine documented window/presence examples are unchanged.
3. The unreadable-window branch obeys the same bound.
4. A measured ceiling below `MIN_COWORKER_ATTACHED_TOOLS` yields a cap equal to that ceiling, and the reason is documented at the floor's definition.
5. The joint invariant is guarded by a test that exercises the budget and the gate ceiling TOGETHER — today `fallback.test.ts` holds zero references to the budget and `coworker-tool-budget.test.ts` pins only a single hardcoded cap-15 case, so the two ends have never been tested against each other.

Provenance: found while auditing whether `BI-A8BFEFCE` fully closed the invariant it introduced, 2026-08-26.

activities.summary: This fix makes BI-95D74DE9 reachable — the always-include set puts a floor of 7 under the attached surface, previously masked by the cap floor of 12

payload.body:
Recorded against this item by the session that raised it, so the consequence travels with the change rather than being discovered later.

Correcting the floor lets a measured tool-fidelity ceiling below 12 be honoured, which is the point. It also allows caps of 4 or 6 for the first time, and that exposes a second bound one layer down.

`selectCoworkerToolBudget` attaches everything in `alwaysIncludeNames` without consulting the cap. Both call sites pass `LOAD_TOOLS_TOOL_NAME` plus the six `AUTHORIZED_SURFACE_TOOL_NAMES`, so the attached surface has a hard floor of 7 regardless of cap:

```
cap=4  -> attached 6 + load_tools = 7  > gate 4
cap=6  -> attached 6 + load_tools = 7  > gate 6
cap=7  -> 7  ok
cap=15 -> 15 ok
```

Below cap 7 the surface is one `callWithFallbackChain` refuses, which is the `BI-A8BFEFCE` failure again. Filed as **`BI-95D74DE9`** with the fix direction — move the surface tools to `pageActionNames` so they keep tier-0 ranking priority but stop being cap-exempt, leaving `load_tools` as the single unconditional entry, which is what this module's own comment already says the contract is.

## Why this PR still stands as-is

The two are separate concerns and separate clean reverts. This change strictly reduces violations: 48 combinations before, zero at the cap level after. The remaining exposure needs a local model measured below 7 — an extreme case that cannot occur today, since no install has measured fidelity at all and every ceiling resolves to the fail-safe cliff of 15.

The honest framing is that this PR does not create a live defect; it removes a mask that was hiding one, and the masked defect is now filed rather than latent and unrecorded.

## Limitation of this PR's guard, worth knowing

The matrix added here asserts `deriveCoworkerToolCap(...) <= resolveLocalToolCeiling(...)`. That is a bound on the derived CAP. It does not exercise `selectCoworkerToolBudget`, so it cannot see the attached-surface floor — which is exactly why `BI-95D74DE9` needed separate discovery. Its acceptance criteria place the assertion on the attached surface, one level below this one.

items.title: Consumer self-upgrade skips because release installs have no Git target
items.body:
## Problem

A Windows consumer/release install can expose self-upgrade as enabled while its configured target source is `/host-dpf`, mapped from `DPF_HOST_INSTALL_PATH`. Consumer installs intentionally contain verified release assets and no `.git` checkout, so manual self-upgrade target resolution repeatedly executes `git -C /host-dpf rev-parse origin/main` and records `skipped / no-target` instead of advancing or reporting that no newer release artifact exists.

Observed on 2026-08-22:
- `.install-mode` is `consumer`; `D:\DPF` has no `.git`.
- `SelfUpgradeRun` rows `SUR-16B67995` and `SUR-16E9F749` are both `skipped`, reason `no-target`, with null current/target/deployed SHA.
- Portal logs report `target-resolution-failed`: `fatal: not a git repository` for `/host-dpf`.
- Platform config stores `hostSourceMountPath: /host-dpf` and defaults `sourceMode` to `upstream`.
- The running image is `821a3f1ca1e5189a01d7a526434c73e650e8ddc6`; upstream main was `6902cb01a6bb2286ca3ac0b5fe4f33a3f2a280d2`; registry `latest` still matched the local digest, so a plain pull could not advance it.
- Installer state was incomplete/stale (`installPath=D:\DPF-cycle2`, empty composeFiles/imageTag/version), making an ad-hoc source-build workaround unsafe.

## Scope

In scope:
- Give consumer/release installs an explicit release-artifact upgrade contract that does not require Git metadata in the install directory.
- Make installer/seed configuration choose the correct source/target resolver for consumer versus contributor installs.
- Preserve the recorded consumer Compose chain and immutable image identity through target resolution, preflight, promotion, and rollback.
- Add an invariant test using a non-Git consumer release-assets fixture.

Out of scope:
- Changing contributor/local source-based self-upgrade behavior.
- Converting consumer install directories into mutable source checkouts.
- Publishing a release artifact as part of this BI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a consumer install with no `.git`, manual self-upgrade never runs Git target resolution against `/host-dpf`.
- [ ] When a newer compatible release artifact exists, the governed path reaches preflight and advances using that immutable artifact while retaining the consumer Compose overlays.
- [ ] When no newer compatible artifact exists, the operator sees an explicit up-to-date/no-published-target result rather than `skipped / no-target`.
- [ ] Installer state contains a valid current install path, compose chain, image tag/version, and deployed identity before self-upgrade is enabled.
- [ ] A regression test covers Windows consumer mode with release assets only and fails if upstream Git mode is selected.
- [ ] Existing contributor upstream/local upgrade tests remain green.

## Dependencies

Independent. Coordinate with PR #4436 (fresh-install reliability) because it also changes installer identity and Compose-chain recording, but do not fold this separate self-upgrade contract into that PR without an explicit scope decision.
